Verdict vs current top 3: Best South American pick: hot, safe (Level 1), great food, wine, museums and Andes hiking. But you spend about 2 of 7 days flying (14h+ each way, 5 hours ahead of LA) for a total about the same as the Big Island. Worth doing on a 10+ night trip, not 7.
Would it make the Ranking tab?: No. It would slot around #6, below Maui and above Joshua Tree + Palm Springs. It doesn't beat or tie any of the top 5.
Flight time & stops (option used in tota: 1 stop each way, about 14.3h fastest outbound (United). Plus a 1.9h nonstop Buenos Aires-Mendoza hop.
January weather (official normals): Buenos Aires: high ~86F / low ~68F, ~9 rain days (Argentina SMN 1991-2020). Mendoza: ~91F / ~67F, ~6 rain days (SMN).
Rainy season?: No. It's summer, with thunderstorms possible in Buenos Aires.
Entry for US citizens: No visa needed for tourist stays
Hikes / museums / food: Aconcagua Provincial Park (Confluencia trail), Cerro Arco; MALBA, Recoleta, Teatro Colon; parrillas, Malbec bodegas in Lujan de Cuyo/Uco Valley
Basis and notes: Flights: Google Flights, cheapest 1-stop LAX-EZE round trip. Domestic: Buenos Aires (AEP)-Mendoza round trip $298 for two (JetSMART nonstop, checked for Jan 5-8). Lodging: Airbnb entire place, Palermo 4n ($431-611/wk p25-p75) + Mendoza 3n ($321-526/wk), times 1.05 est. tax. Transport = domestic flight + taxis/a car day in Mendoza (estimate).

Verdict vs current top 3: Cheapest and warmest South American option (hot, dry Caribbean, old walled city, Tayrona jungle-beach hikes). But Colombia is Level 3 'Reconsider travel', there's no nonstop, and you'd get a similar beach/food/hiking mix in La Paz or Puerto Vallarta in 3h nonstop.
Would it make the Ranking tab?: No. Cost is close to La Paz, but the Level 3 advisory and 12-13h connections put it around #7-8.
Flight time & stops (option used in tota: 1 stop each way, about 13.2h outbound (American, Jan 5-12) / 11.8h (JetBlue, Jan 2-9). The cheapest $964 fare has 2 stops and about 20-22h.
January weather (official normals): Cartagena: high ~88F / low ~75F, ~0 rain days (IDEAM). Santa Marta: ~92F / ~73F, ~0 rain days (IDEAM 1991-2020).
Rainy season?: No. January is peak dry season. Tayrona closes for set periods each year; check the Parques Nacionales calendar before booking.
US State Dept advisory: Level 3: reconsider travel (Mar 31, 2026; crime, terrorism, unrest, kidnapping)
Entry for US citizens: No visa; Check-MIG online form before arrival
Hikes / museums / food: Tayrona Cabo San Juan trail, Minca waterfalls/coffee; Cartagena walled city, Museo del Oro Zenu, Gold Museum Santa Marta; ceviche, arepas, Caribbean seafood
Basis and notes: Lodging: Airbnb, Cartagena 4n ($829-1,297/wk) + Santa Marta 3n ($416-768/wk), times 1.10 est. tax. Transport (estimate): Cartagena-Santa Marta shuttle, taxis, Tayrona entry. Early January is Colombian holiday high season (crowds).

Verdict vs current top 3: Spring-like, not hot. Good food scene, Comuna 13, coffee farms and the Guatape rock climb. Flights cost about 2x Oaxaca for a cooler city, and the Level 3 advisory applies. Oaxaca beats it on every axis.
Flight time & stops (option used in tota: 1 stop, about 11.2h outbound (Avianca). The cheapest $1,838 fare is 1 stop but about 23h.
January weather (official normals): High ~82F / low ~64F, ~8 rain days, January is the driest month (IDEAM 1991-2020, Olaya Herrera)
Rainy season?: No. It's the drier season, but afternoon showers are common.
Hikes / museums / food: Guatape / El Penol, Arvi Park, coffee farm day; Museo de Antioquia (Botero), Casa de la Memoria; bandeja paisa, El Poblado/Laureles restaurants
Basis and notes: Lodging: Airbnb El Poblado $614-891/wk, times 1.10 est. tax. Jan 2-9 cheapest found $2,084 (2 stops, about 20h); Avianca 1-stop $2,386 used.

Verdict vs current top 3: World-class food (Lima) and Machu Picchu. But January is peak rainy season in the Andes (Cusco about 20 rain days, Machu Picchu about 341 mm), 11,000 ft altitude eats a day, and it's cold at night. Not a warm-weather trip. Go May-Sep instead.
Flight time & stops (option used in tota: 1 stop, about 11.8h outbound (Avianca). LATAM nonstop LAX-LIM about 8.7h is $2,942 (Jan 5-12). Plus a 1.3h Lima-Cusco nonstop.
January weather (official normals): Lima: high ~80F / low ~69F, dry (DWD 1991-2020). Cusco: high ~69F / low ~46F, about 20 rain days, 153 mm (NOAA).
Rainy season?: YES in the Andes. January is one of the wettest months. Trains to Machu Picchu often run bus + train; landslides possible. The Inca Trail closes every February.
Hikes / museums / food: Machu Picchu (S/163 for a foreign adult, about $48 at S/3.42 per $), Sacred Valley ruins, Rainbow Mountain; Larco and MALI museums; ceviche, Central/Maido-level dining
Basis and notes: Domestic: Lima-Cusco round trip $272 for two (LATAM nonstop, checked for Jan 3-8). Transport also includes the Machu Picchu train (estimate) and transfers. Lodging: Airbnb Lima 2n ($394-540/wk), Cusco 2n ($258-447/wk), Urubamba 3n ($314-779/wk), times 1.10 est.

Verdict vs current top 3: Spectacular city hikes (Pedra da Gavea, Dois Irmaos, Tijuca) and beaches. But it's the most expensive and longest trip: 15h+ with 1 stop or 23h+ with 2, a required e-visa, very hot and humid with summer storms. Loses to the Big Island on cost and to everything on travel time.
Flight time & stops (option used in tota: 1 stop, about 15.2h outbound (LATAM, Jan 5-12). The cheapest $2,332 fare has 2 stops and is 23h+.
January weather (official normals): High ~89F / low ~75F, about 11 rain days, 137 mm (INMET 1981-2010)
Rainy season?: Partly. It's summer, with frequent afternoon thunderstorms.
Entry for US citizens: E-VISA REQUIRED: US$80.90 per person via VFS Global (required since Apr 10, 2025; get it before buying flights)
Hikes / museums / food: Pedra da Gavea, Dois Irmaos, Tijuca Forest, Sugarloaf; Museum of Tomorrow, MAR, Escadaria Selaron; churrasco, botecos, feijoada
Basis and notes: Lodging: Airbnb Copacabana p25 $599 to Ipanema p75 $1,271 per week, times 1.05 est. Jan 2-9: $2,946 with 2 stops / $3,512 with 1 stop (used).

Flight time & stops (option used in tota: 1 stop, about 14.5-18h outbound (American). No nonstop found.

Hikes / museums / food: Cajon del Maipo / El Morado glacier hike, Cerro San Cristobal; Museo de la Memoria, Pre-Columbian Art Museum; Casablanca/Maipo wineries, Valparaiso seafood
